subject: Political Science
text:
In the question given below, there are two statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read the statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): Killings and atrocities were committed by both sides during partition of India.
Reason (R): The planned transfer of population between India and Pakistan failed. (2026 Board)
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are false
explanation: Both are true: atrocities were committed by both sides, and the population transfer was chaotic and unplanned. The failure of planned transfer led to the violence and killings.
whyWrong: R does explain A — the absence of orderly transfer contributed to violence.
A is true — communal violence occurred on both sides.
Both statements are factually accurate.

subject: Political Science
text: On which date did NITI Aayog come into existence, replacing the Planning Commission? (2026 Board)
explanation: NITI Aayog was established on 1st January 2015, when the Planning Commission was dissolved on 31st December 2014.
whyWrong: 15th August 2014 was Independence Day — NITI Aayog was not established then.
26th January 2015 is Republic Day — NITI Aayog was established on 1st January.
2nd October 2014 is Gandhi Jayanti — NITI Aayog was not established then.

subject: Political Science
text:
Arrange the following events related to planning in India in chronological order:
(i) K.N. Raj presented draft First Five Year Plan
(ii) Bombay Plan presented by industrialists
(iii) Planning Commission established
(iv) Mahalanobis presented the Second Five Year Plan
Choose the correct sequence: (2026 Board)
explanation: Bombay Plan (1944), Planning Commission (1950), K.N. Raj's First FYP draft (1951), Mahalanobis Second FYP (1955-56).
whyWrong: Bombay Plan preceded Planning Commission.
Mahalanobis Plan was last, not first.
Planning Commission came before K.N. Raj's FYP draft.

subject: Political Science
text: Which alliance implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations in 1990? (2026 Board)
explanation: The National Front government under V.P. Singh implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations in August 1990, reserving 27% of central government jobs for OBCs.
whyWrong: UPA governed 2004-2014 — Mandal was implemented in 1990.
NDA has not been associated with Mandal Commission implementation.
Janata Dal was the party but the government was National Front coalition.

subject: Political Science
text: Which political party has 'Gandhian Socialism' and 'cultural nationalism' as its ideology? (2026 Board)
explanation: BJP combines its Hindu nationalist (cultural nationalism) ideology with elements of Gandhian Socialism, making it unique among Indian parties.
whyWrong: Congress follows Gandhian socialism but not cultural nationalism as defined here.
CPI follows Marxist-Leninist ideology, not Gandhian socialism.
Janata Party was a broad coalition without a unified ideology.

subject: Political Science
text: [SAARC Passage] Which of the following was NOT a founding member of SAARC? (2026 Board)
explanation: SAARC was founded in 1985 with 7 members: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and Maldives. Afghanistan joined later in 2007.
whyWrong: India is a founding member of SAARC.
Pakistan is a founding member of SAARC.
Bangladesh is a founding member of SAARC.

subject: Political Science
text: [SAARC Passage] Which external power has most influenced South Asian affairs? (2026 Board)
explanation: The USA has had the most significant influence on South Asian politics — through Cold War alliances with Pakistan, economic aid, and post-9/11 engagement in Afghanistan.
whyWrong: China has growing influence but historically USA has had more impact on South Asian politics.
Russia/Soviet Union had influence during Cold War but less than USA.
UK's influence was historical (colonial), but USA has had greater recent influence.

subject: Political Science
text: [SAARC Passage] What is the major objective of SAARC? (2026 Board)
options: Promote military cooperation among South Asian countries
Establish a common currency for South Asia
Create a military alliance against China
Cooperate for economic growth, social progress, and cultural development
explanation: SAARC's charter states its purpose is to accelerate economic growth, social progress, and cultural development through collective action and mutual assistance.
whyWrong: Military cooperation is not SAARC's primary objective.
Common currency is not a SAARC goal.
SAARC is not a military alliance.

subject: Political Science
text: [SAARC Passage] Which of the following is NOT a core objective of SAFTA (South Asian Free Trade Area)? (2026 Board)
options: Establish a common currency for South Asia
Reduce tariffs on goods traded within SAARC
Create a free trade zone in South Asia
explanation: SAFTA aims to reduce tariffs and promote free trade within SAARC. Creating a common currency is not part of SAFTA's objectives.
whyWrong: Reducing tariffs is a core SAFTA objective.
Promoting trade and economic cooperation is a core SAFTA objective.
Creating a free trade zone is SAFTA's primary goal.

subject: Political Science
text: [UN Security Council Reform Passage] Which UN organ has 5 permanent members with veto power? (2026 Board)
explanation: The UN Security Council has 5 permanent members (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) each with veto power, plus 10 non-permanent elected members.
whyWrong: General Assembly has all 193 member states with equal vote, no veto.
Secretariat is the administrative body headed by Secretary General.
ICJ has 15 judges; no state has veto power over it.

subject: Political Science
text: [UN Security Council Reform Passage] Which country contributes most to the UN budget? (2026 Board)
explanation: The USA is the largest contributor to the UN budget, contributing approximately 22% of the regular budget and 27% of the peacekeeping budget.
whyWrong: China is the second largest contributor but less than USA.
Germany contributes significantly but less than USA.
Japan is a major contributor but less than USA.

subject: Political Science
text: [UN Security Council Reform Passage] In which year were the number of non-permanent members of UNSC increased from 6 to 10? (2026 Board)
explanation: The UN Charter was amended in 1965 to increase non-permanent UNSC members from 6 to 10, reflecting the expansion of UN membership due to decolonisation.
whyWrong: 1955 is not the year of this expansion.
1960 was the 'Year of Africa' with many new UN members, but expansion happened in 1965.
1963 is not the year of UNSC expansion.

subject: Political Science
text: [UN Security Council Reform Passage] Which of the following is NOT correct about the UN Security Council? (2026 Board)
options: It has primary responsibility for international peace and security
P5 members have the right to veto any substantive resolution
Non-permanent members are elected for two-year terms
The Security Council maintains a large standing army
explanation: The UNSC does not have its own standing army. It authorises member states or regional organisations to deploy troops for peacekeeping missions.
whyWrong: UNSC does have primary responsibility for peace and security — correct.
P5 do have veto power on substantive resolutions — correct.
Non-permanent members are elected for 2-year terms — correct.

subject: Political Science
text: [Bandung Conference Passage] Which Indian leader championed Afro-Asian unity? (2026 Board)
explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was the prime architect of Afro-Asian solidarity and NAM, attending the Bandung Conference in 1955 and championing anti-colonialism.
whyWrong: Patel focused on internal integration of India, not foreign policy leadership.
Ambedkar was focused on constitutional and social reform, not foreign policy.
Radhakrishnan was a philosopher and later President, not foreign policy leader.

subject: Political Science
text: [Bandung Conference Passage] In which year did NAM become the symbol of Afro-Asian unity? (2026 Board)
explanation: The first NAM Summit in Belgrade in 1961 marked NAM becoming the symbol of Afro-Asian unity, with newly independent nations asserting their independence from Cold War blocs.
whyWrong: 1955 was the Bandung Conference (Afro-Asian Conference), not NAM summit.
1956 was not a landmark year for NAM.
1964 was the second NAM summit in Cairo.

subject: Political Science
text: [Bandung Conference Passage] What was the core idea behind Afro-Asian unity in the Cold War period? (2026 Board)
options: Create a military alliance against colonialism
Join the Western bloc to counter Soviet influence
Join the Soviet bloc to counter Western imperialism
Maintain distance from both superpowers and pursue independent foreign policy
explanation: The core idea of NAM and Afro-Asian unity was to maintain independence from both Cold War blocs — neither aligning with USA nor USSR — and pursuing an independent foreign policy.
whyWrong: NAM was not a military alliance.
Joining the Western bloc would be alignment, opposite of NAM.
Joining the Soviet bloc would be alignment, opposite of NAM.

subject: Political Science
text: [India-China Relations Passage] In which year did China annex Tibet? (2026 Board)
explanation: China occupied and annexed Tibet in 1950, which became a source of tension with India since Tibet had previously acted as a buffer state between India and China.
whyWrong: 1947 was India's independence year, not China's Tibet annexation.
1954 was when Panchsheel was signed, not Tibet annexation.
1962 was the Sino-Indian war, not Tibet annexation.

subject: Political Science
text: [India-China Relations Passage] Which Tibetan spiritual leader sought political asylum in India? (2026 Board)
explanation: The 14th Dalai Lama fled Tibet in 1959 and was granted political asylum by India, establishing a government-in-exile in Dharamsala, which became a source of China-India tension.
whyWrong: Panchen Lama remained in Tibet under Chinese authority.
Rinpoche is a title, not a specific person who sought asylum.
Karmapa sought asylum later; the key figure in Sino-Indian relations is the Dalai Lama.

subject: Political Science
text: [India-China Relations Passage] Which agreement was jointly signed by India and China in 1954? (2026 Board)
explanation: The Panchsheel Agreement (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was signed between India and China in 1954, laying the foundation for peaceful bilateral relations.
whyWrong: Simla Agreement (1972) was between India and Pakistan, not China.
Delhi Declaration is not the correct name for the 1954 agreement.
The 1954 agreement was called Panchsheel, not 'Treaty of Friendship'.

subject: Political Science
text: [India-China Relations Passage] What was the main reason for the Chinese invasion of India in 1962? (2026 Board)
options: Boundary dispute between India and China
India's alliance with USA against China
explanation: The 1962 Sino-Indian War was primarily over boundary disputes — China claimed Aksai Chin in Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh (then NEFA), while India asserted its own borders.
whyWrong: India's asylum to Dalai Lama was a factor but boundary dispute was the primary cause.
India followed NAM policy — it was not formally allied with USA.
China did not claim Assam — the disputes were over Aksai Chin and NEFA.

subject: Political Science
text: [Congress Party 1989 Passage] In which year did the Congress party first face a significant electoral setback? (2026 Board)
explanation: The 1967 general elections saw Congress's vote share and seats decline significantly; several states saw non-Congress governments for the first time — the first major electoral setback.
whyWrong: 1952 was Congress's triumphant first election.
1977 was a bigger loss but 1967 was the first setback.
1989 was when Congress lost power at centre but 1967 was earlier setback.

subject: Political Science
text: [Congress Party 1989 Passage] Which coalition formed government at the centre in December 1989? (2026 Board)
explanation: After the 1989 elections, the National Front under V.P. Singh formed the first non-Congress government at the centre in December 1989.
whyWrong: UPA was formed in 2004.
NDA was formed in 1998.
United Front was formed in 1996.

subject: Political Science
text: [Congress Party 1989 Passage] Which regional party among the following has NEVER formed a government at the centre? (2026 Board)
explanation: Bharatiya Kranti Dal (BKD) was a regional party that never formed government at the centre. It later merged with the Janata Party.
whyWrong: Telugu Desam Party supported some central governments.
National Conference has had influence at centre through alliance.
DMK has been part of ruling coalitions at centre.

subject: Political Science
text: [Congress Party 1989 Passage] Which was the single largest party after the 1989 general elections? (2026 Board)
explanation: Despite losing its majority, Congress remained the single largest party with 197 seats in the 1989 elections. It chose to sit in opposition, allowing V.P. Singh to form government.
whyWrong: Janata Dal won about 143 seats — fewer than Congress.
BJP won 85 seats in 1989.
CPI(M) won far fewer seats.
